resolution: fixed (27.5) + fixed (30.5) — the arrow detector claims the bare Arrow IPC *stream* framing (a continuation-marked `Schema` message first, then well-formed `RecordBatch`/`DictionaryBatch` messages, ending in an end-of-stream marker) in addition to the file format (magic+footer) and the historical magic+padding-prefixed stream; all four `arrow-stream-*.stream` samples are now claimed as `arrow`. Phase 30.5 adds the legacy pre-0.15 **no-continuation** framing (a bare 4-byte metadata length, a first `Message` header type `Schema` parsed under the bounded reader), gated conservatively by **all-zero** metadata→body padding and an end-of-stream marker that is the **exact** end of the source (so a mixed/re-aligned near-miss still declines). Regression tests `arrow_adapter::stream_framing_is_detected_and_messages_are_ordered_and_exact`, `arrow_adapter::legacy_stream_framing_is_detected_and_built`, `arrow_adapter::stream_near_misses_decline_to_opaque`, `arrow_adapter::legacy_stream_near_misses_decline`; courts `tools/phase27-5-1-arrow-stream-court.sh` and `tools/realformats-stratified-v2-court.sh` (src/adapter/arrow.rs).

fixed (30.5) — `asciidoctor-CHANGELOG.adoc`, `asciidoctor-locale-attributes-ja.adoc`, `asciidoctor-locale-attributes-sr.adoc`, `asciidoctor-pages-macos.adoc`, and `asciidoctor-pages-stylesheet-modes.adoc` are now claimed as AsciiDoc. Each carries an **AsciiDoc-only** mark that reST cannot produce: a column-0 preprocessor/conditional directive (`ifndef::icons[]`/`endif::[]`, `ifdef::listing-caption[…]`, `include::partial$success.adoc[]`) or a block anchor (`[#embed]`). A new narrow predicate `asciidoc::has_asciidoc_only_mark` admits such a source (like the existing `xref:`-macro-list mark), and `rst::looks_like_other` now declines a source carrying the mark so the reST detector does not claim it first. This is **not** a detector reorder — a genuine reST field-list source without the mark is unchanged and reST precedence is preserved. Regression test `asciidoc::tests::detects_asciidoc_only_marks_and_declines_their_negations` (src/adapter/asciidoc.rs, rst.rs).

fixed (28.1) — `asciidoctor-cli-nav.adoc` is now claimed as AsciiDoc. It is a navigation page that is *only* a list of AsciiDoc cross-reference macro calls (`* xref:index.adoc[]`, nested `** xref:man1/asciidoctor.adoc#options[CLI Options]`), which reST and Markdown cannot produce (`xref:target[…]` is an AsciiDoc-only call). A new narrow byte-level signal (`is_xref_macro_list`: ≥2 non-blank lines, every line a list item whose whole text is an `xref:<target>[…]` call) admits it; a plain bullet list without `xref:` macros still stays Opaque. Regression test `asciidoc::tests::detects_a_cross_reference_list_and_declines_its_negations` (src/adapter/asciidoc.rs).

recorded (unchanged reason) — two of the three recorded CBOR declines are genuine detector boundaries and stay recorded: `cbor-data-integer.cbor` is a lone scalar (`18 2a`, 2 bytes) below the deliberate structural bar; `cbor-rfc8949-good.cbor` is a genuinely well-formed single map whose deepest RFC 8949 vector nests to **512 levels**, above the deliberate `max_cbor_depth` cap of 256, so it is declined on the DoS bound (raising that cap to admit one sample is not warranted). The third, `cbor-data-tagged_date.cbor`, is fixed — see the `cbor`/`cbor` note below. The lone-scalar and depth declines are conservative by design (src/adapter/cbor.rs). Phase 30.5 re-attacked both: a lone 2-byte scalar is still below the structural bar (admitting it would widen the CBOR false-positive surface to any two bytes), and the 512-level sample stays above the deliberate DoS depth cap; both remain recorded.

fixed (28.1) — `cbor-data-tagged_date.cbor` (tag 0 around a text date string, 22 bytes) is now claimed as CBOR. A **top-level tag** (major type 6) is itself a strong, self-identifying CBOR construct, so the detector now admits a root tag at `MIN_TAG_DETECT_NODES` (2: the tag plus its one tagged item) rather than requiring the container floor of `MIN_DETECT_NODES` (3); the same bytes without the tag lead are a bare text string (a scalar) and still decline. Regression test `cbor::tests::detects_a_tagged_scalar_and_rejects_a_bare_scalar` (src/adapter/cbor.rs).

recorded decline — `poi-document-Bug60942b.doc` stays here: it is a **Word 6.0** FIB (`wIdent` 0xA5DC, `nFib` 0x0065), outside the supported Word 97-2003 `nFib` subset the adapter models, so it stays at the generic CFBF layer. The second recorded cause, `poi-document-testRangeDelete.doc` (a genuine Word FIB whose `WordDocument` mini-stream is **fragmented** and whose **root mini stream is itself fragmented**), is **fixed (28.1)**: a mini sector's absolute position is now resolved through the root mini stream's FAT chain (`CfbfModel::mini_chain`, added in model version 2), so `cfbf::stream_leading`'s first-chunk prefix read works for a fragmented mini stream; regression test `legacy_cfbf_detection::fragmented_mini_stream_in_fragmented_root_stream_is_detected` (src/adapter/cfbf.rs, doc.rs). Phase 30.5 re-attacked the Word 6.0 decline: admitting `nFib` 0x0065 would require a second FIB/piece-table dialect outside the Word 97–2003 subset, so it stays at the CFBF layer.

recorded decline + fixed (28.1) — `loghub-HPC-HPC_2k.log` stays recorded: it is a space-separated event record with **no timestamp and no level** (`134681 node-246 unix.hw state_change.unavailable …`), which is not a log-stream line grammar and is left to the fixed-width/tabular heuristics.
